Chapter 5

Fields

Motivation: From a vector at a point to a vector at every point

The tangent space \(T_p\mathcal{M}\) lives at a single point, whereas quantities such as a velocity field or the metric vary from point to point. Assigning a vector \(\mathcal{X}_p \in T_p\mathcal{M}\) to every \(p \in \mathcal{M}\), smoothly, requires a single smooth manifold containing all tangent spaces. Their plain union is not one, since it identifies their zero vectors, all equal to the map \(f \mapsto 0\), and carries no charts.

Goal. Make “a smooth assignment of a tensor to every point” precise.

  • Glue the tangent spaces into the tangent bundle \(T\mathcal{M}\), a \(2d\)-dimensional smooth manifold that keeps track of the base point of each vector through a projection \(\pi : T\mathcal{M} \to \mathcal{M}\).

  • Define a vector field as a smooth section of \(T\mathcal{M}\), covector fields likewise through the cotangent bundle, and tensor fields as \(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)-multilinear maps.

  • Since the numbers that rescale fields become scalar fields, fields form \(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)-modules rather than vector spaces, and bases of fields exist in general only locally.

The rest of the notes is formulated with fields. The connection differentiates them, the metric is a tensor field, and the Einstein equations relate tensor fields.
